I am 55 years old. I never went to school, not one day. Everything I know about farming I learned from my mother-in-law and from watching my neighbors. I have been doing this for 30 years. My husband passed away five years ago, so now it is just me and my daughter-in-law handling the 20 mu. We grow cabbage three times a year — spring, summer, and autumn. That is what my mother-in-law did, and that is what Old Li and Old Zhang across the road do too.

I buy my cabbage seedlings from Old Wang at the county market. I get the improved kind, about 3,500 plants per mu. I do not know the name, but I point to the ones that made big heads last year. For fertilizer, I put down two bags of compound fertilizer on every mu — one bag when I am preparing the ground, and another bag about a month later when the heads start forming. Each bag is 50 kg. I also throw in half a bag of urea at topdressing. I know it is a lot, but three years ago my neighbor Liu tried to save money on fertilizer and his cabbage heads were small as fists. The dealer only paid him half price. I would rather waste some fertilizer than face that.

I hire the rotary tiller from the village for all three crops. For water, I irrigate four or five times each crop from my well. The electric pump costs money, but cabbage needs water or the heads crack. In summer I water five times because the sun is fierce. For spraying, I hire the crop protection team. They come about seven or eight times per crop. The summer cabbage gets more because the worms and diseases come with the heat. I tell them when I see caterpillars or spots on the leaves.

Last year my spring cabbage made about 12,000 jin per mu, summer got about 10,000 jin because of the heat, and autumn got 16,000 jin. I hope this year is the same or better. My daughter-in-law says we should grow something else, but I do not know anything else as well as cabbage. At my age, changing crops is too risky. I just do what I did last year, and what my neighbors do.
